title: Churchill gives the Iron Curtain speech
summary: Winston Churchill, speaking at Westminster College in Fulton, Missouri, warned that an iron curtain had descended across Europe. He called for close cooperation between Britain and the United States.
reason: Soviet control was hardening over the states of Eastern Europe occupied by the Red Army, and Churchill wanted to rally American opinion against it.
significance: The speech became one of the defining statements of the early Cold War.
place: Westminster College, Fulton, Missouri, United States

title: The Philippines becomes independent from the United States
summary: The United States recognized the independence of the Philippines in a ceremony in Manila, and the Treaty of Manila was signed the same day. Manuel Roxas became the first president of the independent republic.
reason: The Tydings-McDuffie Act of 1934 had promised independence after a ten year transition, delayed only by the Japanese occupation.
significance: It was one of the first decolonizations of the postwar era in Asia.

title: Direct Action Day riots break out in Calcutta
summary: A general strike called by the Muslim League in Calcutta turned into mass violence between Muslims and Hindus. Thousands of people were killed in the following days.
reason: The Muslim League called the protest to press its demand for a separate Muslim homeland, Pakistan.
significance: The killings made partition of India far more likely.

title: Japan promulgates its postwar constitution
summary: Emperor Hirohito promulgated a new constitution that made sovereignty rest with the people and renounced war in its Article 9. It took effect in May 1947.
reason: The American occupation authorities under Douglas MacArthur pushed for a democratic charter to replace the Meiji Constitution.
significance: It has remained Japan's constitution without a single amendment.

title: Fighting in Hanoi opens the First Indochina War
summary: Viet Minh forces attacked French positions in Hanoi, turning months of tension into open war. Ho Chi Minh and his government withdrew to the countryside.
reason: France sought to restore colonial rule in Indochina, while the Viet Minh had declared Vietnamese independence in 1945.
significance: It began the eight year war that ended French rule in Indochina.

title: Truman announces the Truman Doctrine
summary: President Harry Truman asked Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey and declared that the United States would support free peoples resisting subjugation.
reason: Britain could no longer afford to support Greece against a communist insurgency, and Turkey faced Soviet pressure.
significance: It made containment of communism the core of American foreign policy.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States

title: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan
summary: In a speech at Harvard University, Secretary of State George Marshall proposed large scale American aid to rebuild Europe.
reason: Europe was struggling with hunger and ruined economies, and Washington feared that poverty would help communist parties.
significance: The plan financed Western Europe's recovery and deepened the split with the Soviet bloc.
place: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States

title: Pakistan is created as an independent state
summary: Pakistan came into being as a separate dominion for the Muslim majority areas of British India, with Muhammad Ali Jinnah as governor general.
reason: The Muslim League had demanded a separate homeland, and Britain agreed to partition the subcontinent.
significance: Partition caused one of the largest migrations in history and lasting conflict with India.

title: India becomes independent
summary: At midnight British rule ended and India became an independent dominion, with Jawaharlal Nehru as prime minister. He marked it with his Tryst with Destiny speech.
reason: Decades of nationalist struggle and a Britain exhausted by war led to a quick transfer of power, together with partition.
significance: It ended the British Raj and began the end of European empires in Asia.

title: Kashmir's maharaja accedes to India
summary: Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession to India as tribal fighters from Pakistan advanced toward Srinagar.
reason: The princely state had stayed undecided at partition until the invasion forced the ruler to seek Indian military help.
significance: It began the Kashmir conflict that still divides India and Pakistan.

title: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade is signed
summary: Twenty three countries signed the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade in Geneva, cutting tariffs on a large share of world trade.
reason: Governments wanted to avoid the protectionism that had deepened the Great Depression.
significance: GATT set the rules of world trade until it became the World Trade Organization.
participants: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
wikipedia: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade

title: UN votes to partition Palestine
summary: The United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution 181, recommending that Mandatory Palestine be divided into Jewish and Arab states with Jerusalem under international control.
reason: Britain had given up the mandate, and the UN sought a solution to the conflicting claims of Jews and Arabs.
significance: The vote led directly to the creation of Israel and the first Arab-Israeli war.
place: Flushing Meadows, New York, United States
wikipedia: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine

title: The transistor is demonstrated at Bell Labs
summary: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain, working in William Shockley's group, demonstrated the first working point contact transistor to Bell Labs managers.
reason: Bell Labs wanted a smaller, more reliable replacement for vacuum tubes in telephone amplifiers.
significance: The transistor became the building block of all modern electronics.
place: Bell Labs, Murray Hill, New Jersey, United States

title: Mahatma Gandhi is assassinated
summary: Nathuram Godse, a Hindu nationalist, shot Mahatma Gandhi at Birla House in New Delhi as he walked to a prayer meeting.
reason: Godse blamed Gandhi for partition and for being too accommodating toward Muslims and Pakistan.
significance: The death of the leader of Indian independence shocked the world and discredited militant Hindu nationalism for a time.

title: Assassination of Gaitan sparks the Bogotazo
summary: The popular Liberal leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan was shot in Bogota, setting off riots that destroyed much of the city centre and killed thousands.
reason: Gaitan was the hope of poor Colombians, and political violence between Liberals and Conservatives was already rising.
significance: It opened La Violencia, a decade of civil conflict in Colombia.

title: David Ben-Gurion declares the State of Israel
summary: In Tel Aviv, David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the establishment of the State of Israel, hours before the British Mandate ended. Neighbouring Arab states invaded the next day.
reason: The UN partition plan and the end of British rule opened the way to a Jewish state.
significance: Israel's founding reshaped the Middle East and began the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians.

title: National Party wins South Africa's election
summary: The Afrikaner National Party under Daniel Malan won South Africa's general election on a programme of apartheid.
reason: White voters, especially Afrikaners, feared the growth of black urban populations and backed strict racial separation.
significance: The result began more than four decades of apartheid laws.

title: The Manchester Baby runs the first stored program
summary: The Small-Scale Experimental Machine at the University of Manchester ran its first program, held in its own electronic memory.
reason: Frederic Williams and Tom Kilburn built it to test a new kind of memory based on cathode ray tubes.
significance: It was the first stored program computer, the design of nearly every computer since.
place: University of Manchester, Manchester, United Kingdom

title: The Soviet Union begins the Berlin Blockade
summary: Soviet forces cut all road, rail and canal routes into the western sectors of Berlin. The Western Allies answered with an airlift that supplied the city for almost a year.
reason: Moscow opposed the introduction of a new currency in the western zones and wanted to push the Allies out of Berlin.
significance: It was the first major crisis of the Cold War and hastened the division of Germany.

title: The UN adopts the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
summary: Meeting at the Palais de Chaillot in Paris, the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights without a vote against.
reason: After the atrocities of the Second World War, a committee led by Eleanor Roosevelt drafted a common standard of rights for all peoples.
significance: It became the foundation of international human rights law.

title: The North Atlantic Treaty founds NATO
summary: Twelve countries of North America and Western Europe signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, agreeing that an attack on one would be an attack on all.
reason: The Berlin Blockade and the communist takeover in Czechoslovakia convinced Western governments they needed a military alliance.
significance: NATO became the central Western alliance of the Cold War and after.

title: West Germany's Basic Law is promulgated
summary: The Basic Law, the constitution of the Federal Republic of Germany, was signed and promulgated in Bonn.
reason: The Western Allies wanted a democratic West German state, created from their occupation zones.
significance: It founded West Germany and remains the constitution of reunified Germany.
wikipedia: Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany

title: George Orwell publishes Nineteen Eighty-Four
summary: Secker and Warburg published George Orwell's novel about a totalitarian state that watches and controls its citizens.
reason: Orwell drew on his experience of Stalinism, Nazism and wartime propaganda.
significance: Its words, such as Big Brother, became the vocabulary of debate about surveillance and tyranny.

title: The Geneva Conventions are adopted
summary: A diplomatic conference in Geneva adopted four conventions protecting wounded soldiers, shipwrecked sailors, prisoners of war and civilians in wartime.
reason: The mass killing of civilians and prisoners in the Second World War showed the gaps in earlier treaties.
significance: They are the core of international humanitarian law.
participants: International Committee of the Red Cross

title: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb
summary: The Soviet Union secretly exploded its first atomic bomb, RDS-1, at the Semipalatinsk test site in Kazakhstan.
reason: Stalin had ordered a crash programme after Hiroshima, helped by espionage on the Manhattan Project.
significance: It ended the American nuclear monopoly and started the nuclear arms race.

title: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China
summary: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace in Beijing, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China.
reason: The Communists had won the civil war against Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, who retreated to Taiwan.
significance: It brought the world's most populous country under communist rule.
wikipedia: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

title: The Constitution of India comes into force
summary: India's constitution took effect, turning the dominion into a sovereign republic with Rajendra Prasad as its first president.
reason: A Constituent Assembly chaired in drafting by B. R. Ambedkar had worked since 1946 to give India its own charter.
significance: It made India the largest democracy in the world, marked each year as Republic Day.

title: Robert Schuman proposes pooling coal and steel
summary: French foreign minister Robert Schuman proposed placing French and German coal and steel production under a common authority open to other European countries.
reason: Jean Monnet's plan aimed to make another war between France and Germany materially impossible.
significance: It is seen as the founding act of European integration, marked as Europe Day.

title: North Korea invades South Korea
summary: North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel in a full scale invasion of South Korea, quickly advancing toward Seoul.
reason: Kim Il Sung wanted to unify Korea by force and had won the approval of Stalin and Mao.
significance: The Korean War drew in the United States, the UN and China and froze the division of Korea.

title: Japan signs the Treaty of San Francisco
summary: Japan and 48 nations signed the peace treaty that formally ended the Second World War in the Pacific and restored Japan's sovereignty.
reason: The United States wanted Japan as a Cold War ally and pushed for a quick, lenient peace.
significance: It ended the occupation and shaped the postwar order in East Asia.
place: War Memorial Opera House, San Francisco, United States

title: Police kill students in Dhaka's Language Movement
summary: Police opened fire on students in Dhaka protesting for Bengali to be an official language of Pakistan, killing several.
reason: The Pakistani government planned to make Urdu the sole national language, though most East Pakistanis spoke Bengali.
significance: The day is remembered worldwide as International Mother Language Day and fed Bangladeshi nationalism.

title: Free Officers overthrow King Farouk
summary: The Free Officers Movement, led by Mohamed Naguib and Gamal Abdel Nasser, seized power in Egypt and forced King Farouk to abdicate.
reason: Officers were angered by corruption, British influence and Egypt's defeat in the 1948 war.
significance: It began an era of Arab nationalism led by Nasser.

title: Britain declares an emergency in Kenya
summary: The colonial governor declared a state of emergency in Kenya and arrested Jomo Kenyatta and other nationalist leaders.
reason: The Mau Mau movement among the Kikuyu was attacking settlers and loyalists over land and colonial rule.
significance: The brutal counterinsurgency that followed hastened the end of British rule in East Africa.

title: The United States detonates the first hydrogen bomb
summary: The United States exploded Ivy Mike, the first full scale thermonuclear device, on Elugelab island in Enewetak Atoll, which was vaporized.
reason: After the first Soviet atomic test, Truman ordered development of a far more powerful weapon.
significance: It raised the nuclear arms race to weapons of almost unlimited power.

title: The Great Smog descends on London
summary: A thick smog of coal smoke and fog covered London for five days, bringing transport to a halt. It is now thought to have caused about 10,000 deaths.
reason: Cold, windless weather trapped smoke from homes, factories and power stations burning coal.
significance: It led to the Clean Air Act of 1956 and modern pollution control.

title: Joseph Stalin dies
summary: Soviet leader Joseph Stalin died at his dacha at Kuntsevo near Moscow, days after a stroke.
reason: Stalin was 74 and had been in failing health.
significance: His death opened a power struggle and a gradual thaw in the Soviet Union.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Joseph Stalin

title: Watson and Crick publish the structure of DNA
summary: Nature published James Watson and Francis Crick's paper proposing the double helix structure of DNA, alongside papers from King's College London.
reason: Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images and Maurice Wilkins' work gave the evidence the Cambridge pair used to build their model.
significance: It explained how genetic information is copied and founded molecular biology.
wikipedia: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid

title: Hillary and Tenzing reach the summit of Everest
summary: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay, a Sherpa from Nepal, became the first people known to reach the top of Mount Everest.
reason: A large British expedition led by John Hunt had chosen them for the second summit attempt.
significance: It was the climax of the race for the world's highest peak.

title: The Korean Armistice ends the fighting in Korea
summary: Delegates of the UN Command, North Korea and the Chinese volunteers signed an armistice at Panmunjom, creating a demilitarized zone.
reason: Two years of stalemate and Stalin's death made both sides ready to stop fighting.
significance: No peace treaty followed, so Korea remains divided and technically at war.

title: A CIA backed coup ousts Iran's Mosaddegh
summary: Royalist officers and street crowds organized with American and British help overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh, restoring the shah's power.
reason: Mosaddegh had nationalized the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, and Washington feared a communist drift.
significance: The coup shaped Iranian anger at the West that erupted in 1979.

title: Dien Bien Phu falls to the Viet Minh
summary: After a siege of nearly two months, the French garrison at Dien Bien Phu in northern Vietnam surrendered to Viet Minh forces under Vo Nguyen Giap.
reason: France had fortified the remote valley to lure the Viet Minh into battle, but Giap surrounded it with artillery on the hills.
significance: The defeat ended French rule in Indochina and sent shock waves through colonial empires.

title: US Supreme Court rules school segregation unconstitutional
summary: In Brown v. Board of Education, the Supreme Court unanimously ruled that racial segregation in public schools violated the Constitution.
reason: The NAACP, led in court by Thurgood Marshall, had challenged the separate but equal doctrine for years.
significance: The ruling was a turning point of the civil rights movement.
participants: Supreme Court of the United States
place: Supreme Court Building, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Obninsk becomes the first nuclear plant to power a grid
summary: The nuclear power plant at Obninsk near Moscow was connected to the electricity grid, the first in the world to do so.
reason: Soviet scientists wanted to show a peaceful use of atomic energy.
significance: It began the age of civil nuclear power.

title: Guatemala's President Arbenz is forced out
summary: President Jacobo Arbenz resigned after an invasion by exiles organized by the CIA, ending Guatemala's democratic revolution.
reason: Arbenz's land reform had taken unused land of the United Fruit Company, and Washington saw communist influence.
significance: The coup began decades of military rule and civil war in Guatemala.

title: Geneva Accords divide Vietnam
summary: The Geneva Conference ended with agreements that divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel and confirmed the independence of Laos and Cambodia.
reason: France wanted out of Indochina after Dien Bien Phu, and the great powers sought a settlement.
significance: The temporary division of Vietnam led to the Vietnam War.

title: The FLN launches the Algerian War
summary: The National Liberation Front carried out a wave of coordinated attacks across Algeria, known as Red All Saints' Day.
reason: Algerian nationalists had lost hope of reform after decades of French settler rule.
significance: It began the war that ended with Algerian independence in 1962.

title: Salk's polio vaccine is declared safe and effective
summary: At the University of Michigan, researchers announced that a huge field trial had shown Jonas Salk's polio vaccine to be safe and effective.
reason: Polio epidemics paralysed thousands of children each year, and the March of Dimes funded the trial.
significance: Mass vaccination began, and polio was eventually eliminated in most of the world.
place: University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, United States

title: The Bandung Conference opens
summary: Leaders of 29 Asian and African countries met at Bandung in Indonesia to promote cooperation and oppose colonialism.
reason: Newly independent states wanted a voice outside the rival Cold War blocs.
significance: It laid the ground for the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: The Warsaw Pact is signed
summary: The Soviet Union and seven Eastern European states signed a treaty of mutual defence in Warsaw.
reason: Moscow answered West Germany's entry into NATO with an alliance of its own.
significance: It bound the Eastern bloc militarily to Moscow until 1991.

title: The Congress of the People adopts the Freedom Charter
summary: At Kliptown near Johannesburg, the Congress of the People adopted the Freedom Charter, declaring that South Africa belongs to all who live in it.
reason: The African National Congress and its allies wanted a common programme against apartheid.
significance: The charter became the founding document of the anti-apartheid movement.

title: Rosa Parks refuses to give up her bus seat
summary: Rosa Parks, a Black seamstress and NAACP activist, was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, for refusing to give her bus seat to a white passenger.
reason: Montgomery's buses enforced racial segregation, and activists were looking for a case to challenge it.
significance: Her arrest started the Montgomery bus boycott and brought Martin Luther King Jr. to the fore.

title: Khrushchev denounces Stalin in the Secret Speech
summary: At a closed session of the 20th Party Congress, Nikita Khrushchev condemned Stalin's personality cult and crimes.
reason: Khrushchev wanted to break with terror and strengthen his position against Stalin's old associates.
significance: The speech shook communist movements worldwide and encouraged unrest in Eastern Europe.
participants: Communist Party of the Soviet Union
wikipedia: On the Cult of Personality and Its Consequences

title: Nasser nationalizes the Suez Canal
summary: In a speech in Alexandria, Gamal Abdel Nasser announced the nationalization of the Suez Canal Company.
reason: The United States and Britain had withdrawn funding for the Aswan High Dam, and Nasser wanted canal revenue to pay for it.
significance: It led to the Suez Crisis, which marked the end of Britain and France as imperial powers in the Middle East.

title: B. R. Ambedkar converts to Buddhism with his followers
summary: In Nagpur, B. R. Ambedkar and several hundred thousand followers, mostly Dalits, converted to Buddhism.
reason: Ambedkar rejected Hinduism's caste system, which had made his community untouchable.
significance: It started a large Buddhist revival among India's Dalits.

title: The Hungarian Revolution begins
summary: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a national uprising against the communist government and Soviet control. Soviet forces crushed it in November.
reason: Khrushchev's denunciation of Stalin and the Polish October encouraged Hungarians to demand reform and freedom.
significance: It showed that Moscow would use force to keep its bloc together.

title: Ghana becomes independent
summary: The Gold Coast became independent as Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, the first sub-Saharan African colony to win independence from colonial rule after the war.
reason: Nkrumah's Convention People's Party had won elections and pressed Britain for self-government.
significance: It inspired independence movements across Africa.

title: The Treaty of Rome creates the European Economic Community
summary: Six Western European countries signed the Treaty of Rome, founding the European Economic Community and Euratom.
reason: After the coal and steel community, governments wanted a common market to drive growth and bind Europe together.
significance: The EEC grew into the European Union.

title: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1
summary: The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite, from Baikonur. Its radio beeps were heard around the world.
reason: Sergei Korolev's team used the new R-7 missile to beat the United States into orbit during the International Geophysical Year.
significance: It began the Space Age and the space race.

title: Brazil wins its first World Cup with a teenage Pele
summary: Brazil beat hosts Sweden 5 to 2 in the World Cup final in Solna. Seventeen year old Pele scored twice.
reason: Brazil's team combined new tactics with brilliant young players.
significance: It began Brazil's era as the leading football nation and made Pele a star.

title: The 14 July Revolution overthrows Iraq's monarchy
summary: Army officers led by Abd al-Karim Qasim seized Baghdad and killed King Faisal II and much of the royal family.
reason: Many Iraqis resented the pro-Western monarchy and its Baghdad Pact, inspired by Nasser's Arab nationalism.
significance: It ended Iraq's Hashemite monarchy and the Baghdad Pact's centre.

title: Jack Kilby demonstrates the first integrated circuit
summary: At Texas Instruments in Dallas, Jack Kilby demonstrated a working circuit built on a single piece of germanium.
reason: Engineers were looking for a way around the tangle of wires needed to connect many separate components.
significance: The integrated circuit made microchips and modern computing possible.
place: Texas Instruments, Dallas, Texas, United States

title: Batista flees as the Cuban Revolution triumphs
summary: Dictator Fulgencio Batista fled Cuba in the early hours of the new year, and Fidel Castro's rebels took power.
reason: Castro's guerrillas had won key battles, and Batista had lost the support of the army and of Washington.
significance: It brought a communist state to the Western Hemisphere.

title: The Tibetan uprising begins in Lhasa
summary: Crowds surrounded the Norbulingka palace in Lhasa to protect the Dalai Lama from feared arrest by Chinese authorities. The revolt was crushed and the Dalai Lama fled to India.
reason: Tibetans resented Chinese rule since 1950 and reforms imposed in eastern Tibet.
significance: It began the Tibetan exile in India and remains a defining moment for Tibet.

title: Students begin the Greensboro sit-ins
summary: Four Black students sat at the whites only lunch counter of a Woolworth's store in Greensboro, North Carolina, and refused to leave.
reason: Young activists were frustrated by the slow pace of desegregation.
significance: The sit-in movement spread across the South and led to the founding of SNCC.
place: Woolworth store, Greensboro, North Carolina, United States

title: Police kill 69 protesters at Sharpeville
summary: South African police opened fire on a crowd protesting the pass laws at Sharpeville, killing 69 people.
reason: The Pan Africanist Congress had called for protesters to turn up at police stations without their passes.
significance: The massacre led to the banning of the ANC and PAC and the turn to armed struggle.

title: Brasilia is inaugurated as Brazil's capital
summary: President Juscelino Kubitschek inaugurated Brasilia, a new capital built on the central plateau in under four years.
reason: Kubitschek wanted to develop the interior, and Lucio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer designed the city.
significance: It is a landmark of modernist architecture and city planning.

title: Theodore Maiman builds the first laser
summary: At Hughes Research Laboratories in Malibu, Theodore Maiman operated the first working laser, using a ruby crystal.
reason: Physicists were racing to build an optical maser after the theory was published in 1958.
significance: Lasers became essential in medicine, communications and industry.
place: Hughes Research Laboratories, Malibu, California, United States

title: The strongest earthquake ever recorded hits Chile
summary: A magnitude 9.5 earthquake struck southern Chile, the most powerful ever measured. Its tsunami crossed the Pacific to Hawaii and Japan.
reason: It occurred where the Nazca Plate dives under the South American Plate.
significance: It killed thousands and shaped the study of great earthquakes and tsunami warnings.

title: Congo becomes independent from Belgium
summary: The Belgian Congo became independent as the Republic of the Congo, with Patrice Lumumba as prime minister. Within days the army mutinied.
reason: Riots in 1959 led Belgium to grant independence quickly and with little preparation.
significance: It opened the Congo Crisis, a central Cold War conflict in Africa.
place: Leopoldville (Kinshasa), Democratic Republic of the Congo

title: Sirimavo Bandaranaike becomes the world's first woman prime minister
summary: Sirimavo Bandaranaike was sworn in as prime minister of Ceylon after leading her party to election victory.
reason: She took over the Sri Lanka Freedom Party after her husband, Prime Minister S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike, was assassinated.
significance: She was the first woman elected head of government in the modern world.

title: OPEC is founded in Baghdad
summary: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela founded the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.
reason: Western oil companies had cut posted prices, reducing the revenues of producing states.
significance: OPEC gave oil states great power over the world economy.

title: The trial of Adolf Eichmann opens in Jerusalem
summary: Adolf Eichmann, a chief organizer of the Holocaust captured by Israeli agents in Argentina, went on trial in Jerusalem.
reason: Israel wanted to try him for crimes against the Jewish people and make the Holocaust known.
significance: The televised trial made survivors' testimony heard around the world.

title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
summary: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once in Vostok 1, a flight of 108 minutes.
reason: The Soviet Union wanted to beat the United States in putting a person into space.
significance: It opened human spaceflight and spurred the American push for the Moon.

title: The Bay of Pigs invasion fails
summary: About 1,400 Cuban exiles trained by the CIA landed at the Bay of Pigs and were defeated by Castro's forces within three days.
reason: Washington wanted to overthrow Castro without openly using American troops.
significance: The failure strengthened Castro and pushed Cuba toward the Soviet Union.

title: Amnesty International is launched
summary: Lawyer Peter Benenson published an article in The Observer appealing for the release of prisoners of conscience, which began Amnesty International.
reason: Benenson was angered by the jailing of two Portuguese students for a toast to freedom.
significance: It grew into one of the leading human rights organizations.

title: East Germany starts building the Berlin Wall
summary: Overnight East German troops and workers sealed the border between East and West Berlin with barbed wire, soon replaced by a wall.
reason: Millions of East Germans had fled to the West through Berlin, draining the country of skilled workers.
significance: The wall became the symbol of the Cold War division of Europe.

title: The Evian Accords end the Algerian War
summary: France and the Algerian provisional government signed agreements at Evian-les-Bains, providing a ceasefire and a vote on independence.
reason: After eight years of war, de Gaulle decided France could not keep Algeria.
significance: Algeria became independent in July 1962, and about a million settlers left.
participants: Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic

title: Rachel Carson publishes Silent Spring
summary: Houghton Mifflin published Rachel Carson's book documenting the harm caused by pesticides such as DDT.
reason: Carson, a marine biologist, was alarmed by the effects of widespread spraying on wildlife.
significance: It started the modern environmental movement.

title: The Second Vatican Council opens
summary: Pope John XXIII opened the Second Vatican Council in St. Peter's Basilica, with about 2,500 bishops attending.
reason: John XXIII wanted to bring the Church up to date with the modern world.
significance: It transformed Catholic worship, including mass in local languages, and relations with other faiths.

title: The Cuban Missile Crisis begins
summary: President Kennedy was shown photographs proving that the Soviet Union was building nuclear missile sites in Cuba. Thirteen days of confrontation followed.
reason: Khrushchev placed missiles in Cuba to protect Castro and offset American missiles near the Soviet Union.
significance: It was the closest the world came to nuclear war.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: China attacks India, starting the Sino-Indian War
summary: Chinese forces launched offensives against Indian positions in the eastern Himalayas and Aksai Chin, routing Indian troops within weeks.
reason: The two countries disputed their border, and India's Forward Policy and its shelter for the Dalai Lama angered Beijing.
significance: The defeat shocked India and left a border dispute that still remains.
place: Namka Chu valley, near Tawang, India

title: The Organisation of African Unity is founded
summary: Leaders of 32 independent African states founded the Organisation of African Unity at a summit in Addis Ababa.
reason: African states wanted unity against colonialism and apartheid and to settle disputes among themselves.
significance: It was the forerunner of the African Union, and the date is marked as Africa Day.

title: Monk Thich Quang Duc burns himself in Saigon
summary: The Buddhist monk Thich Quang Duc set himself on fire at a busy Saigon intersection. Photographs of his death went around the world.
reason: Buddhists were protesting the persecution of their religion by Ngo Dinh Diem's Catholic dominated government.
significance: It undermined American support for Diem.

title: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space
summary: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova was launched in Vostok 6 and orbited the Earth 48 times in nearly three days.
reason: The Soviet programme wanted another first, choosing her from a group of women parachutists.
significance: She remains the only woman to have flown a solo space mission.

title: The Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty is signed
summary: The United States, the Soviet Union and Britain signed a treaty in Moscow banning nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in space and under water.
reason: The Cuban Missile Crisis and fears about fallout made the powers seek limits.
significance: It was the first major treaty to restrain the nuclear arms race.

title: Martin Luther King Jr. gives his I Have a Dream speech
summary: About 250,000 people joined the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom, where Martin Luther King Jr. gave his I Have a Dream speech.
reason: Civil rights groups wanted to press Congress to pass Kennedy's civil rights bill.
significance: It became a defining moment of the civil rights movement.
place: Lincoln Memorial, Washington, D.C., United States
wikipedia: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom

title: John F. Kennedy is assassinated in Dallas
summary: President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed while riding in a motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas. Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested for the murder.
reason: Oswald, a former Marine who had lived in the Soviet Union, fired from the Texas School Book Depository.
significance: The killing shocked the world and Lyndon Johnson became president.
place: Dealey Plaza, Dallas, Texas, United States

title: The Beatles appear on The Ed Sullivan Show
summary: The Beatles performed live on The Ed Sullivan Show in New York, watched by about 73 million Americans.
reason: Their records had just topped the American charts, and the visit was heavily promoted.
significance: It launched the British Invasion of American pop music.
place: Ed Sullivan Theater, New York City, United States
wikipedia: The Beatles in the United States

title: The military overthrows Brazil's President Goulart
summary: Brazilian army units rebelled against President Joao Goulart, who fled to Uruguay within days.
reason: Conservatives and the military feared Goulart's reforms and left wing allies, and Washington supported the plotters.
significance: It began 21 years of military dictatorship in Brazil.

title: Mandela is sentenced to life at the Rivonia Trial
summary: Nelson Mandela and seven other ANC leaders were sentenced to life imprisonment for sabotage in Pretoria.
reason: The apartheid government sought to destroy the ANC's armed resistance.
significance: The trial made Mandela a world symbol of resistance to apartheid.
place: Palace of Justice, Pretoria, South Africa

title: Lyndon Johnson signs the Civil Rights Act
summary: President Lyndon Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, banning discrimination based on race, colour, religion, sex or national origin.
reason: The civil rights movement and Kennedy's death created momentum to overcome Southern opposition in Congress.
significance: It ended legal segregation in public places in the United States.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: The Gulf of Tonkin incident
summary: North Vietnamese torpedo boats attacked the US destroyer Maddox in the Gulf of Tonkin. A second attack reported two days later probably never happened.
reason: The Maddox was gathering intelligence near North Vietnam's coast during South Vietnamese raids.
significance: Congress's resolution after the incident allowed the American escalation of the Vietnam War.
place: Gulf of Tonkin, off North Vietnam

title: The Shinkansen bullet train opens
summary: The Tokaido Shinkansen between Tokyo and Osaka opened, the first high speed railway line in the world.
reason: Japan needed more capacity on its busiest corridor and wanted to showcase recovery before the Olympics.
significance: It started the age of high speed rail.

title: Singapore becomes independent
summary: Singapore separated from Malaysia and became an independent republic. Lee Kuan Yew wept as he announced it.
reason: Tensions between Singapore's Chinese majority leadership and the Malay led federal government made the union unworkable.
significance: The city state became one of the world's richest countries.

title: The 30 September Movement tries to seize power in Indonesia
summary: Army officers calling themselves the 30 September Movement killed six generals in Jakarta. General Suharto crushed them and blamed the Communist Party.
reason: Tensions between the army and the Communist Party under Sukarno's rule had reached a crisis.
significance: It led to mass killings of perhaps 500,000 people and Suharto's three decades of rule.

title: Mao launches the Cultural Revolution
summary: The Communist Party Politburo issued the May 16 Notification, attacking hidden bourgeois enemies and opening the Cultural Revolution.
reason: Mao Zedong wanted to regain power after the failure of the Great Leap Forward and purge rivals in the party.
significance: A decade of upheaval followed, with persecution, violence and millions of deaths.

title: Biafra declares independence from Nigeria
summary: Military governor Odumegwu Ojukwu declared the Eastern Region of Nigeria independent as the Republic of Biafra.
reason: Massacres of Igbo people in the north after the 1966 coups convinced Igbo leaders they were unsafe in Nigeria.
significance: The civil war that followed caused a famine that killed perhaps a million people.

title: Israel strikes Egypt, starting the Six-Day War
summary: Israel launched surprise air strikes that destroyed most of Egypt's air force on the ground, then fought Egypt, Jordan and Syria.
reason: Egypt had expelled UN peacekeepers, closed the Straits of Tiran and massed troops in Sinai.
significance: Israel captured Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, East Jerusalem and the Golan Heights, reshaping the conflict.

title: ASEAN is founded in Bangkok
summary: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand signed the Bangkok Declaration, founding the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.
reason: The countries wanted regional stability and economic cooperation while the Vietnam War raged.
significance: ASEAN became the main regional organization of Southeast Asia.

title: Che Guevara is executed in Bolivia
summary: Che Guevara, captured the day before, was executed by the Bolivian army in the village of La Higuera.
reason: Guevara tried to start a guerrilla war in Bolivia, but the army, aided by the CIA, hunted down his band.
significance: He became an international icon of revolution.

title: Christiaan Barnard performs the first human heart transplant
summary: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, Christiaan Barnard transplanted the heart of a young woman into Louis Washkansky.
reason: Surgeons had worked toward transplants on animals for years.
significance: It opened the field of heart transplantation.
place: Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa

title: North Vietnam launches the Tet Offensive
summary: North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces attacked cities and bases across South Vietnam during the Tet holiday, even entering the US embassy compound in Saigon.
reason: Hanoi hoped to spark a popular uprising and break American resolve.
significance: Though a military defeat for the attackers, it turned American opinion against the war.
participants: Army of the Republic of Vietnam

title: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated
summary: Martin Luther King Jr. was shot dead on a balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis by James Earl Ray.
reason: King was in Memphis to support striking sanitation workers.
significance: His death set off riots in more than 100 American cities.
place: Lorraine Motel, Memphis, Tennessee, United States
wikipedia: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.

title: The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty is opened for signature
summary: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons was opened for signature in Washington, London and Moscow.
reason: The nuclear powers feared that many more countries would build the bomb.
significance: It became the cornerstone of efforts to limit the spread of nuclear weapons.
wikipedia: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons

title: Warsaw Pact troops invade Czechoslovakia
summary: Soviet and allied Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia overnight to end the Prague Spring reforms of Alexander Dubcek.
reason: Moscow feared that freedom of speech and reform would spread through its bloc.
significance: It crushed hopes of reform communism for two decades.

title: Mexican troops fire on students at Tlatelolco
summary: Soldiers and police opened fire on a student rally in the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Mexico City, killing many.
reason: The government wanted to end student protests before the Olympics opened ten days later.
significance: It became a lasting symbol of state repression in Mexico.
place: Plaza de las Tres Culturas, Mexico City, Mexico

title: Tommie Smith and John Carlos raise their fists at the Olympics
summary: On the medal podium of the 200 metres in Mexico City, American sprinters Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised black gloved fists.
reason: They protested racial injustice in the United States.
significance: The image became one of the most famous political gestures in sport.
place: Estadio Olimpico Universitario, Mexico City, Mexico

title: Apollo 8 launches the first crewed flight to the Moon
summary: Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders were launched to become the first people to orbit the Moon, where they took the Earthrise photograph.
reason: NASA moved the mission forward fearing a Soviet circumlunar flight.
significance: It was the first time humans left Earth's orbit and saw the whole planet.
place: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

title: The Stonewall riots begin in New York
summary: A police raid on the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in Greenwich Village, set off days of protests and clashes.
reason: Gay people in New York faced frequent police raids and harassment.
significance: Stonewall became the starting point of the modern LGBT rights movement.
place: Stonewall Inn, New York City, United States

title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle on the Sea of Tranquility, and Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon.
reason: President Kennedy had set the goal of a Moon landing within the decade, in the space race with the Soviet Union.
significance: It was the first time humans set foot on another world.

title: Muammar Gaddafi seizes power in Libya
summary: A group of young army officers led by Muammar Gaddafi overthrew King Idris in a bloodless coup.
reason: The officers, inspired by Nasser, opposed the pro-Western monarchy and foreign oil companies.
significance: Gaddafi ruled Libya for 42 years.

title: ARPANET sends its first message
summary: Student programmer Charley Kline at UCLA sent the first message over ARPANET to the Stanford Research Institute. The system crashed after the letters L and O.
reason: The US Defense Department's ARPA funded a network to share computing resources among research centres.
significance: ARPANET was the forerunner of the Internet.
place: University of California, Los Angeles, United States

title: The first Earth Day is held
summary: About 20 million Americans took part in rallies and teach-ins for the environment on the first Earth Day.
reason: Senator Gaylord Nelson organized it after oil spills and growing concern about pollution.
significance: It helped bring about American environmental laws and became a worldwide event.

title: The Bhola cyclone strikes East Pakistan
summary: A tropical cyclone and storm surge struck the coast of East Pakistan, killing several hundred thousand people.
reason: The low lying Ganges delta was exposed to the storm, and warnings and relief were inadequate.
significance: Anger at the government's response helped lead to the independence of Bangladesh.

title: Pakistan's army launches Operation Searchlight
summary: The Pakistani army began a crackdown in Dhaka against Bengali nationalists, killing students, intellectuals and civilians.
reason: The Awami League had won the 1970 election, and West Pakistan's leaders refused to hand over power.
significance: It started the Bangladesh Liberation War.

title: Nixon ends the dollar's convertibility into gold
summary: President Nixon announced that the United States would no longer convert dollars into gold, along with wage and price controls.
reason: American inflation and trade deficits had made the fixed exchange rate system of Bretton Woods unsustainable.
significance: It ended the Bretton Woods system and began floating exchange rates.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: The UN gives China's seat to the People's Republic
summary: The UN General Assembly voted to recognize the People's Republic of China as the only legitimate representative of China, expelling the Republic of China.
reason: A growing number of states recognized Beijing, and the United States was moving toward detente with China.
significance: It brought mainland China into the UN and its Security Council.
place: United Nations Headquarters, New York, United States

title: Pakistan surrenders in Dhaka and Bangladesh is born
summary: General A. A. K. Niazi signed the surrender of Pakistani forces in East Pakistan to the Indian and Bangladeshi forces at the Ramna Race Course in Dhaka.
reason: India had entered the war in December after months of refugees and fighting.
significance: It confirmed the independence of Bangladesh.

title: Richard Nixon arrives in China
summary: President Nixon landed in Beijing and met Mao Zedong, the first visit by an American president to the People's Republic.
reason: Both sides wanted to balance the Soviet Union, and Henry Kissinger had prepared the visit in secret.
significance: It transformed the Cold War balance of power.
wikipedia: 1972 visit by Richard Nixon to China

title: Nixon and Brezhnev sign the SALT I agreements
summary: In Moscow, Nixon and Leonid Brezhnev signed the Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty and an interim agreement limiting strategic missiles.
reason: Both powers wanted to slow the costly arms race in an era of detente.
significance: It was the first agreement to limit American and Soviet strategic weapons.

title: Burglars are arrested at the Watergate complex
summary: Five men linked to Nixon's re-election campaign were arrested breaking into the Democratic National Committee offices at the Watergate building.
reason: Nixon aides wanted to spy on his political opponents.
significance: The cover-up led to Nixon's resignation.
participants: Committee for the Re-Election of the President
place: Watergate complex, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Terrorists take Israeli athletes hostage at the Munich Olympics
summary: Members of the Palestinian group Black September seized Israeli team members in the Olympic Village. Eleven Israelis were killed.
reason: The group demanded the release of Palestinian prisoners held in Israel.
significance: It was a turning point in international terrorism and counterterrorism.

title: Roe v. Wade legalizes abortion in the United States
summary: The US Supreme Court ruled that the Constitution protected a woman's right to choose abortion.
reason: Abortion was banned in most states, and the case challenged a Texas law.
significance: It shaped American politics for half a century until it was overturned in 2022.
participants: Supreme Court of the United States
place: Supreme Court Building, Washington, D.C., United States

title: The Paris Peace Accords are signed
summary: The United States, North Vietnam, South Vietnam and the Viet Cong's government signed agreements in Paris to end the Vietnam War.
reason: Years of negotiation and Nixon's need to withdraw American troops led to the deal.
significance: American forces left Vietnam, but fighting between the Vietnamese resumed.

title: Martin Cooper makes the first handheld mobile phone call
summary: Motorola engineer Martin Cooper called a rival at Bell Labs from a prototype handheld phone on a New York street.
reason: Motorola was competing with AT&T to develop cellular telephone technology.
significance: It began the era of mobile phones.
place: Sixth Avenue, New York City, United States

title: Pinochet's coup overthrows Salvador Allende
summary: The Chilean armed forces led by Augusto Pinochet bombed La Moneda palace, where President Allende died.
reason: Economic crisis, polarization and American hostility to Allende's socialism led the military to act.
significance: It began 17 years of dictatorship in Chile.

title: Egypt and Syria attack Israel on Yom Kippur
summary: Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israel on the holiest day of the Jewish year, crossing the Suez Canal and entering the Golan Heights.
reason: Egypt and Syria wanted to win back territory lost in 1967.
significance: The war led to the oil embargo and later to peace between Egypt and Israel.

title: Arab oil producers announce an oil embargo
summary: Arab members of OPEC meeting in Kuwait decided to cut oil production, followed by an embargo on the United States and other supporters of Israel.
reason: They wanted to punish Western support for Israel in the Yom Kippur War.
significance: Oil prices quadrupled, causing recession and changing energy policy worldwide.
participants: Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries

title: The Carnation Revolution topples Portugal's dictatorship
summary: Junior army officers overthrew the Estado Novo regime in a nearly bloodless coup, with crowds placing carnations in soldiers' rifles.
reason: Officers were weary of colonial wars in Africa, and the regime had refused reform.
significance: It brought democracy to Portugal and independence to its African colonies.

title: India conducts its first nuclear test
summary: India exploded a nuclear device, code named Smiling Buddha, underground at Pokhran in the Rajasthan desert.
reason: India wanted to show its strength after China's nuclear tests and the 1971 war.
significance: It made India the first country outside the UN's permanent members to test a nuclear weapon.

title: Richard Nixon resigns the presidency
summary: Richard Nixon became the only US president to resign, leaving office as Gerald Ford was sworn in.
reason: Tapes proved Nixon's role in covering up the Watergate break-in, and impeachment was certain.
significance: It showed that the president was not above the law.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: The fossil Lucy is discovered in Ethiopia
summary: Donald Johanson and Tom Gray found a 3.2 million year old partial skeleton of Australopithecus afarensis at Hadar, Ethiopia.
reason: Paleoanthropologists were searching the Afar region for early human ancestors.
significance: Lucy showed that human ancestors walked upright long before brains grew large.

title: The Lebanese Civil War begins
summary: Christian Phalangist gunmen attacked a bus carrying Palestinians in the Beirut suburb of Ain el-Rummaneh, after an attack on a church. Fighting spread across Lebanon.
reason: Tensions among religious communities and the armed Palestinian presence had undermined Lebanon's power sharing system.
significance: The war lasted 15 years and killed about 150,000 people.

title: The Khmer Rouge capture Phnom Penh
summary: Khmer Rouge forces entered Phnom Penh and soon emptied the city, driving its people into the countryside.
reason: The Khmer Rouge had won the civil war against the American backed Khmer Republic.
significance: Their regime killed about 1.5 to 2 million Cambodians.

title: Saigon falls to North Vietnam
summary: North Vietnamese tanks broke through the gates of the Independence Palace in Saigon, and South Vietnam surrendered.
reason: After the American withdrawal, the South Vietnamese army collapsed in a spring offensive.
significance: It ended the Vietnam War and unified Vietnam under communist rule.
place: Independence Palace, Saigon (Ho Chi Minh City), Vietnam

title: The Helsinki Final Act is signed
summary: Thirty five states, including the United States and the Soviet Union, signed the Final Act of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe.
reason: The Soviet Union sought recognition of postwar borders, and the West won human rights commitments in return.
significance: Its rights provisions became a tool for dissidents in the Eastern bloc.
participants: Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe

title: Argentina's military overthrows Isabel Peron
summary: Argentina's armed forces ousted President Isabel Peron and installed a junta led by Jorge Videla.
reason: Political violence, economic chaos and a weak government gave the military its pretext.
significance: The junta's Dirty War made tens of thousands of people disappear.

title: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak found Apple
summary: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer to sell Wozniak's Apple I computer.
reason: Wozniak had designed a simple computer board for hobbyists, and Jobs saw a business.
significance: Apple helped launch the personal computer revolution.

title: Students rise up in Soweto
summary: Police opened fire on thousands of Black students protesting in Soweto against being taught in Afrikaans. Hundreds died in the uprising.
reason: Students rejected a decree forcing Afrikaans as a language of instruction, seen as the language of the oppressor.
significance: It gave new life to the struggle against apartheid.

title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
summary: NASA's Viking 1 lander touched down on Mars and sent back the first photographs from the planet's surface.
reason: NASA wanted to study Mars and search for signs of life.
significance: It was the first fully successful landing on Mars.

title: The Tangshan earthquake devastates northern China
summary: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake destroyed the industrial city of Tangshan in the early morning, killing at least 240,000 people.
reason: It struck a fault beneath the city with no warning while people slept.
significance: It was one of the deadliest earthquakes of the 20th century.

title: Mao Zedong dies
summary: Mao Zedong, leader of the People's Republic of China since 1949, died in Beijing.
reason: Mao was 82 and had suffered from ill health.
significance: His death led to the fall of the Gang of Four and opened the way to Deng Xiaoping's reforms.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Mao Zedong

title: Voyager 1 is launched
summary: NASA launched Voyager 1 from Cape Canaveral to fly past Jupiter and Saturn. It carried the Golden Record of sounds from Earth.
reason: A rare alignment of the outer planets made a grand tour possible.
significance: It became the first spacecraft to reach interstellar space.

title: Steve Biko dies in police custody
summary: Black Consciousness leader Steve Biko died in a Pretoria prison after being beaten by security police.
reason: Biko was arrested under apartheid security laws for his political activism.
significance: His death brought world condemnation and an arms embargo on South Africa.

title: Anwar Sadat visits Jerusalem
summary: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat flew to Israel and the next day addressed the Knesset, the first Arab leader to visit the country.
reason: Sadat wanted to recover Sinai and end the cost of war with Israel.
significance: It opened the way to the Camp David Accords.

title: Communists seize power in Afghanistan
summary: Officers loyal to the People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan attacked the presidential palace in Kabul and killed President Mohammed Daoud Khan.
reason: Daoud had cracked down on the communist party and arrested its leaders.
significance: Revolt against the new regime led to the Soviet invasion and decades of war.

title: Louise Brown, the first IVF baby, is born
summary: Louise Brown, the first person conceived by in vitro fertilization, was born at Oldham General Hospital in England.
reason: Robert Edwards and Patrick Steptoe had worked for years to help infertile couples conceive.
significance: IVF has since led to millions of births.
place: Oldham General Hospital, Oldham, United Kingdom

title: Egypt and Israel sign the Camp David Accords
summary: After 13 days of talks at Camp David, Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin signed frameworks for peace at the White House, witnessed by Jimmy Carter.
reason: Sadat's visit to Jerusalem and Carter's mediation brought the leaders together.
significance: They led to the Egypt and Israel peace treaty of 1979.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Karol Wojtyla is elected Pope John Paul II
summary: Cardinal Karol Wojtyla of Krakow was elected pope, the first non-Italian in 455 years.
reason: The cardinals sought a strong leader after John Paul I died after only 33 days.
significance: His papacy encouraged opposition to communism in Poland.

title: Deng Xiaoping launches China's reform and opening up
summary: The Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee opened in Beijing and shifted the party's focus to economic modernization under Deng Xiaoping.
reason: After Mao's death and the chaos of the Cultural Revolution, Deng won the struggle for leadership.
significance: The reforms turned China into an economic superpower.

title: Ayatollah Khomeini returns to Iran
summary: Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returned to Tehran after 14 years in exile, welcomed by millions. Within ten days the old regime collapsed.
reason: Mass protests had forced the shah to leave Iran in January.
significance: It led to the founding of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

title: Margaret Thatcher becomes Britain's first woman prime minister
summary: Margaret Thatcher became prime minister the day after her Conservative Party won the general election.
reason: Strikes during the Winter of Discontent had discredited the Labour government.
significance: Her free market policies reshaped Britain and influenced the world.

title: Students seize the US embassy in Tehran
summary: Iranian students stormed the American embassy in Tehran and took 52 Americans hostage, holding them for 444 days.
reason: They demanded that the United States return the shah, who had been admitted for medical treatment.
significance: The crisis ended Jimmy Carter's presidency and poisoned relations between Iran and the United States.
participants: Muslim Student Followers of the Imam's Line

title: Militants seize the Grand Mosque in Mecca
summary: Armed militants led by Juhayman al-Otaybi seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca, holding it for two weeks.
reason: They accused the Saudi royal family of corruption and proclaimed one of their number the Mahdi.
significance: The Saudi state responded by empowering conservative clerics.

title: Soviet forces storm the palace in Kabul
summary: Soviet special forces stormed the Tajbeg Palace and killed Afghan leader Hafizullah Amin as Soviet troops poured into Afghanistan.
reason: Moscow distrusted Amin and feared the collapse of the communist government facing revolt.
significance: It began the Soviet war in Afghanistan, which drained the Soviet Union.

title: Archbishop Oscar Romero is assassinated
summary: Archbishop Oscar Romero of San Salvador was shot dead while celebrating mass in a hospital chapel.
reason: Romero had denounced the army's killings and called on soldiers to stop the repression.
significance: His murder pushed El Salvador into civil war, and he was later declared a saint.

title: The WHO declares smallpox eradicated
summary: The World Health Assembly in Geneva declared that smallpox had been eradicated, the first human disease wiped out.
reason: A global vaccination and surveillance campaign since 1967 had tracked down the last cases.
significance: It is one of the greatest achievements of public health.

title: The Gwangju Uprising begins
summary: Students and citizens in Gwangju rose against South Korea's military rulers after paratroopers attacked protesters. The army crushed the uprising, killing hundreds.
reason: General Chun Doo-hwan had seized power and extended martial law.
significance: It became a central memory of South Korea's struggle for democracy.

title: The Gdansk Agreement legalizes free trade unions
summary: Poland's government and striking shipyard workers led by Lech Walesa signed an agreement allowing independent trade unions.
reason: A strike at the Lenin Shipyard over prices and a fired worker spread across the country.
significance: It created Solidarity, the first independent union in the Soviet bloc.

title: The first Space Shuttle flight is launched
summary: Space Shuttle Columbia lifted off from Kennedy Space Center with John Young and Robert Crippen on the first orbital flight of a reusable spacecraft.
reason: NASA wanted a reusable vehicle to lower the cost of reaching orbit.
significance: The shuttle flew for 30 years and built the International Space Station.
place: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

title: The CDC reports the first cases of what became AIDS
summary: The US Centers for Disease Control reported five cases of a rare pneumonia among young gay men in Los Angeles.
reason: Doctors had noticed unusual infections that pointed to a collapse of the immune system.
significance: It marked the start of the HIV/AIDS pandemic.
participants: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: IBM launches the IBM Personal Computer
summary: IBM introduced its Personal Computer, using an Intel processor and Microsoft's operating system.
reason: IBM wanted a quick entry into the growing personal computer market and used outside parts.
significance: Its open design became the industry standard for personal computers.

title: Anwar Sadat is assassinated
summary: Islamist army officers shot Egyptian President Anwar Sadat during a military parade in Cairo.
reason: The Egyptian Islamic Jihad group condemned his peace with Israel and his crackdown on opponents.
significance: Hosni Mubarak succeeded him and ruled for 30 years.

title: The Syrian army besieges Hama
summary: Syrian forces besieged the city of Hama to crush an uprising by the Muslim Brotherhood, killing thousands of people.
reason: Hafez al-Assad's regime faced years of Islamist attacks and wanted to end the revolt.
significance: It was among the deadliest acts of an Arab state against its own people.

title: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands
summary: Argentine forces landed on the Falkland Islands and forced the small British garrison at Stanley to surrender.
reason: Argentina's military junta claimed the islands and hoped to win popular support amid economic crisis.
significance: Britain retook the islands, and defeat brought down Argentina's junta.

title: Massacre at Sabra and Shatila
summary: Lebanese Christian militiamen killed hundreds of Palestinian and Lebanese civilians in the Sabra and Shatila camps in Beirut, which Israeli forces had surrounded.
reason: The militia sought revenge for the assassination of its leader, President-elect Bashir Gemayel.
significance: An Israeli inquiry found Ariel Sharon indirectly responsible.

title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP
summary: ARPANET switched permanently to the TCP/IP protocols, allowing different networks to connect to one another.
reason: Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn had designed TCP/IP to link many separate networks.
significance: It is often seen as the birth of the Internet.

title: Benigno Aquino is assassinated at Manila airport
summary: Opposition leader Benigno Aquino Jr. was shot dead as he left the plane on his return from exile.
reason: Aquino came back to challenge Ferdinand Marcos's dictatorship.
significance: His murder united the opposition that overthrew Marcos in 1986.

title: Soviet fighter shoots down Korean Air Lines Flight 007
summary: A Soviet interceptor shot down a Korean Air Lines Boeing 747 that had strayed into Soviet airspace, killing all 269 people aboard.
reason: The airliner had drifted off course, and Soviet air defence took it for a spy plane.
significance: It sharpened Cold War tensions and led the United States to open GPS to civilian use.
place: Near Moneron Island, Sea of Japan, Russia

title: Apple launches the Macintosh
summary: Steve Jobs unveiled the Macintosh, a personal computer with a graphical interface and a mouse, at a shareholders' meeting in Cupertino.
reason: Apple wanted an easy to use computer to compete with IBM.
significance: It made the graphical user interface popular.
place: Flint Center, Cupertino, California, United States

title: Indira Gandhi is assassinated
summary: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was shot dead by two of her Sikh bodyguards in the garden of her residence in New Delhi.
reason: The bodyguards acted in revenge for the army assault on the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
significance: Her murder was followed by massacres of Sikhs in Delhi.

title: Gas leak at Bhopal kills thousands
summary: Toxic methyl isocyanate gas leaked from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, killing thousands of people overnight.
reason: Poor maintenance and failing safety systems allowed water to enter a storage tank.
significance: It is the world's worst industrial disaster.

title: Britain and China agree on Hong Kong's return
summary: Margaret Thatcher and Zhao Ziyang signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration in Beijing, agreeing that Hong Kong would return to China in 1997.
reason: Britain's lease on the New Territories ran out in 1997, and Deng Xiaoping insisted on full sovereignty.
significance: It set the terms of one country, two systems for Hong Kong.
place: Great Hall of the People, Beijing, China

title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes Soviet leader
summary: The Communist Party chose Mikhail Gorbachev as general secretary, a day after the death of Konstantin Chernenko.
reason: After a series of aged leaders, the party turned to a younger reformer.
significance: His reforms of glasnost and perestroika led to the end of the Cold War.
participants: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

title: Scientists report the ozone hole over Antarctica
summary: Joseph Farman, Brian Gardiner and Jonathan Shanklin of the British Antarctic Survey published evidence in Nature of severe ozone loss over Antarctica.
reason: Measurements at Halley station showed a seasonal drop in ozone linked to CFC gases.
significance: It led directly to the Montreal Protocol.

title: Live Aid concerts raise money for Ethiopia
summary: Benefit concerts at Wembley Stadium in London and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia were broadcast to an estimated 1.9 billion people.
reason: Bob Geldof and Midge Ure organized it to raise funds for victims of the Ethiopian famine.
significance: It was one of the largest television broadcasts ever.

title: Earthquake devastates Mexico City
summary: A magnitude 8.0 earthquake off the Pacific coast collapsed buildings across Mexico City, killing at least 5,000 people.
reason: The city's soft lake bed soils amplified the shaking.
significance: Citizen rescue efforts after the slow official response strengthened civil society in Mexico.

title: Mudflows bury the Colombian town of Armero
summary: An eruption of the Nevado del Ruiz volcano melted its ice cap, and mudflows buried the town of Armero, killing over 20,000 people.
reason: Warnings from scientists went unheeded, and the town was not evacuated.
significance: It became a lesson in volcanic hazard management.

title: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks up after launch
summary: Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after lift-off, killing all seven crew, including teacher Christa McAuliffe.
reason: A rubber O-ring seal in a booster rocket failed in the cold weather.
significance: It halted the shuttle programme for almost three years.
place: Off Cape Canaveral, Florida, United States

title: People Power drives Ferdinand Marcos from power
summary: After four days of mass protests on EDSA avenue in Manila, Ferdinand Marcos fled and Corazon Aquino was sworn in as president.
reason: Marcos had claimed victory in a fraudulent election, and part of the army turned against him.
significance: It restored democracy and inspired peaceful movements elsewhere.

title: Reactor explodes at Chernobyl
summary: Reactor No. 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear plant in Soviet Ukraine exploded during a safety test, releasing radioactive material across Europe.
reason: A flawed reactor design and operators breaking rules during the test caused a power surge.
significance: It is the worst nuclear disaster in history and damaged trust in the Soviet system.
place: Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, Pripyat, Ukraine

title: Reagan and Gorbachev meet at Reykjavik
summary: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev met at Hofdi House in Reykjavik and came close to agreeing to abolish nuclear weapons.
reason: Both leaders wanted to reduce the arms race, though they split over missile defence.
significance: It paved the way for the INF Treaty.

title: The Montreal Protocol is signed
summary: Countries meeting in Montreal signed a protocol to phase out CFCs and other chemicals destroying the ozone layer.
reason: The discovery of the ozone hole showed the danger of these chemicals.
significance: It is regarded as the most successful environmental treaty.

title: Reagan and Gorbachev sign the INF Treaty
summary: At the White House, Reagan and Gorbachev signed a treaty eliminating all American and Soviet intermediate range nuclear missiles.
reason: The deployment of missiles in Europe in the early 1980s had alarmed both sides.
significance: It was the first treaty to abolish a whole class of nuclear weapons.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: The First Intifada begins
summary: Palestinian protests broke out in the Jabalia refugee camp in Gaza and spread across the occupied territories.
reason: A traffic accident that killed four Palestinians sparked anger built up over twenty years of occupation.
significance: The uprising put the Palestinian cause at the centre of world attention and led toward the Oslo Accords.

title: Iraq attacks Halabja with chemical weapons
summary: Iraqi aircraft dropped chemical weapons on the Kurdish town of Halabja, killing about 5,000 civilians.
reason: Saddam Hussein's regime was punishing Kurds who had sided with Iran in the war.
significance: It is the deadliest chemical attack against civilians in history.

title: The 8888 Uprising challenges Burma's military regime
summary: A general strike and mass demonstrations against one party military rule spread across Burma. The army crushed them weeks later.
reason: Economic collapse and student protests had built up anger against Ne Win's regime.
significance: It brought Aung San Suu Kyi to the head of the democracy movement.

title: Chileans vote No to Pinochet
summary: In a national plebiscite, Chileans rejected another eight years of rule by Augusto Pinochet.
reason: The 1980 constitution required a vote, and a broad opposition campaigned for No.
significance: It led to free elections and the return of democracy in 1990.

title: Yasser Arafat proclaims a State of Palestine
summary: The Palestine National Council meeting in Algiers adopted a declaration of independence for a State of Palestine.
reason: The First Intifada and Jordan's withdrawal of its claim to the West Bank pushed the PLO to act.
significance: It implied PLO acceptance of a two state solution.

title: Pan Am Flight 103 is bombed over Lockerbie
summary: A bomb destroyed Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, killing 270 people in the air and on the ground.
reason: Libyan intelligence agents were later convicted of planting the bomb.
significance: It was the deadliest terrorist attack in British history.

title: Khomeini issues a fatwa against Salman Rushdie
summary: Ayatollah Khomeini called on Muslims to kill author Salman Rushdie over his novel The Satanic Verses.
reason: Many Muslims considered the novel blasphemous toward the Prophet Muhammad.
significance: It became a global clash over free expression and religion.

title: The last Soviet troops leave Afghanistan
summary: General Boris Gromov walked across the Friendship Bridge into Soviet Uzbekistan, the last Soviet soldier to leave Afghanistan.
reason: After a decade of war with mujahideen, Gorbachev decided to withdraw under the Geneva Accords.
significance: It ended a war that drained the Soviet Union and left Afghanistan in civil war.

title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web
summary: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee submitted a proposal for an information system linking documents with hypertext.
reason: Scientists at CERN struggled to share information across different computers.
significance: It led to the World Wide Web.
wikipedia: History of the World Wide Web

title: Troops crush the Tiananmen Square protests
summary: Chinese troops and tanks cleared Tiananmen Square and surrounding streets in Beijing, killing hundreds or more protesters.
reason: Students and workers had occupied the square for weeks, demanding political reform and an end to corruption.
significance: It ended the democracy movement in China.

title: Two million people form the Baltic Way
summary: About two million people joined hands in a human chain across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
reason: They marked 50 years since the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, which had led to Soviet occupation.
significance: It drew world attention to the Baltic independence movements.

title: The Berlin Wall falls
summary: After a confused announcement of new travel rules, crowds of East Berliners pushed through the border crossings and began tearing down the wall.
reason: Mass protests and emigration had shaken East Germany, and Moscow would not intervene.
significance: It symbolized the end of the Cold War and led to German reunification.

title: The Velvet Revolution begins in Prague
summary: Police beat students marching in Prague on International Students' Day, sparking mass protests that ended communist rule within weeks.
reason: Revolutions elsewhere in Eastern Europe encouraged Czechoslovaks to demand change.
significance: Vaclav Havel became president, and the transition was peaceful.

title: Nicolae Ceausescu is executed
summary: Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceausescu and his wife Elena were shot after a hasty military trial in Targoviste.
reason: A revolution that began in Timisoara had overthrown the regime, and the army had changed sides.
significance: It was the only violent overthrow of a communist regime in Eastern Europe in 1989.
